name: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd
title: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Ltd - 544286 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Document is a Q4 FY25 earnings call transcript, not the Q2 FY27 outcome named in the request; FY25 combined ratio ex-1/N 96.1% and expense of management 37.4% are the usable numbers, and no prior-guidance items are repeated.

red_flags.label: Document period mismatch: Q4 FY25 call supplied for Q2 FY27 request

evasions.topic: Hospital empanelment and common network status

evasions.quote: We are happy to share that offline.

summary.headline: Niva Bupa FY25 like-to-like GWP grew 32% to Rs.7,406 crore; IFRS PAT rose 91% to Rs.203 crore, with combined ratio 96.1% ex-1/N.
summary.overview: This is the FY25 (Q4) results call, held after the company's November 2024 listing, and the metadata labels it Q2 FY27, which conflicts with the content. Management stressed like-to-like figures because of the 1/N accounting change effective October 1, 2024, which lowered reported growth to 21% (GWP) and raised the reported combined ratio to 101.2%. Profitability improved: IFRS PAT rose to Rs.203 crore and iGAAP profit to Rs.214 crore, with expense of management down to 37.4%. Q&A focused on claims inflation (ACS about 5%), loss ratio drift in retail (65% to 66%), network hospital strategy, industry negative press, and the 1/N effect on multi-year and affinity products.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: About 65.5% of FY25 GWP; retail market share rose to 9.4% from 9.1%. Retail IFRS loss ratio rose about 100 bps to 66% from 65%.

segments.name: Group (B2B, employer-employee, B2B2C affinity)
segments.commentary: Group is about 13% employer-employee and about 22% affinity; group share rose to about 12–12.5% from about 10%, mainly from two large corporate accounts. Combined group IFRS loss ratio rose to 58.2% from 57.7%.

segments.name: Rise product (new, Feb 2025)
segments.commentary: Launched in the last quarter of FY25 to target the 'Missing Middle' segment; no premium or volume data disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of reaching the allowable expense ratio of 35.5% in FY26, about 190 bps below the FY25 level of 37.4%.
Target renewal book loss ratio is about 75%, which management said the company is currently within.
Common empanelment initiative led by the General Insurance Council is in progress, with pushback from hospitals.
Guidance for FY26 and FY27 was deferred to offline discussion.
capex_capacity: Network of about 10,500 hospitals, with 80%+ of claims from a few hundred hospitals; network growth deliberately restrained.
Preferred Provider Network (PPN) covers about 600 hospitals in 40 cities and takes at least 15% of claims in those cities, rising.
demand_pricing: Medical (claim) inflation as average claim size growth was about 5% in FY25 versus about 7.4% in FY24, in line with the 5–6.5% range seen historically.
Annual premium revisions (about 10% in recent years per analyst question) are used to pass on medical inflation.

Management says the industry is growing double digit and Niva Bupa grew over 30%. It attributes negative press to perception rather than data, citing improving claim settlement ratios and lower complaints per 10,000 policies and claims.
Multi-year (three-year) share of retail was about 20%, slightly lower than last year because the 1/N accounting changes distributor remuneration timing.
Port-in share of retail health is in the 20s percent, unchanged.
Retail lives grew about 18% in FY25. Less than 2% of onboarding customers are declined for lack of an appropriate product.
Steady-state retail claim incidence is seen at 7–7.5%, and the current level is below that. Employer-employee incidence is 2.5–3 pp higher than retail, mainly due to maternity.

qa_highlights.question: Split of loss ratio across retail and group, and how employer-employee volatility is being managed; what is different about claim inflation (down from about 7.4% to 5%) versus industry trends?
qa_highlights.answer: IFRS loss ratio was 63.8% in FY25 (63.0% in FY24) including about 3 pp claims handling loading; retail 66% vs 65%, group 58.2% vs 57.7%. Management cited five levers: risk selection (lifetime value), risk pricing (diabetics priced at 1.5–2x average lifetime cost), claims management, cross-sell and annual premium revision.

qa_highlights.question: Expense of management glide path to the regulatory limit and network hospital growth and common empanelment status.
qa_highlights.answer: EoM fell to 37.4% from 39.3% and 41.2% over two years; allowable ratio is 35.5%, so about 190 bps still to go, which management is confident of closing in FY26. Network growth was a conscious choice. The common empanelment initiative is work in progress with pushback from hospitals.

qa_highlights.question: Is negative industry news affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industry data show better claim settlement ratios and fewer complaints per 10,000 claims and policies, so the issue is perception. Ankur Kharbanda said the industry and Niva Bupa (over 30% growth) are still growing and that the Council plans a PR and awareness drive.

qa_highlights.question: Why has group health grown faster and what is the outlook? Is AUM growth changing the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Group growth came from two large corporate accounts won in the last quarter, lifting group share to 12–12.5%. AUM rose faster mainly due to the primary IPO capital raise; excluding that, it is in line with GWP growth.

qa_highlights.question: Group health split and multi-year (three-year) share; port-in share; affinity competition; other income in shareholder account.
qa_highlights.answer: Of total book, about 65% retail, 13% employer-employee, and the rest benefit-based, indemnity, PA, with affinity about 22%. Multi-year share is about 20%. Port-in share is in the 20s, with no material change. Competitors entered affinity, but Niva Bupa added more accounts, partners and lines in the last six months. Other income of Rs.11.9 crore came from recovery of earlier written-off debts (IIFL, RCap).

qa_highlights.question: Claims reserves (outstanding plus IBNR) as a share of net claims fell from about 67% to 61%; is the reserve base being reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the annual IBNR plus outstanding ratio is unchanged, and quarterly movement reflects infection seasonality. Earlier conservatism was released because the feared claim rebound did not happen. Adequacy is tested every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Investment book mix and product and fraud-related changes to reduce claim leakage.
qa_highlights.answer: The investment book is almost entirely debt, with a negligible NIFTY ETF holding. Product changes include deductibles from Rs.10,000–20,000 up to Rs.5 lakh and analytics-driven fraud triggers. Management said it would share fraud-prevention numbers offline.

risks_watch: Retail loss ratio rose about 100 bps to 66%, and steady-state incidence is above the current level, so loss ratios may drift up as the book matures.
Industry-wide negative press on claim rejections, hospital tie-ups and third-party investigations; management says it is perception-driven, but it could affect demand.
Hospital pushback on the common empanelment initiative led by the General Insurance Council.
The 1/N accounting change lowers reported growth and reduces distributor remuneration timing, which could slow multi-year cover sales.
Reserve ratio (outstanding plus IBNR to net claims) fell about 6 pp QoQ; the company says this is seasonal, but the trend needs watching.
Guidance for FY26 and FY27 was not given on the call.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the structural story and the expense ratio trajectory, but defensive about industry perception and claim incidence. Management avoided quantifying guidance and deferred several questions (FY26–27 guidance, fraud metrics, cohort loss ratios) offline.
key_quotes: So we closed last year in terms of GWP at Rs.7,406 crores, a growth rate of 32% without the "1/N" accounting change.
So we are very confident that we will be able to achieve this in current financial year looking at the trajectory.
Ultimately the focus of all of this is to manage to a target claims ratio and we deploy broadly five levers to do that .

growth.why: Brief describes FY25 Q4 results (metadata says Q2 FY27, conflicting); FY26/FY27 guidance was deferred offline, with only an expense ratio target of 35.5% in FY26 and no capacity additions or quantified revenue guidance, so backing is none.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management is confident of reaching the 35.5% allowable expense ratio in FY26, about 190 bps below the FY25 level of 37.4%, while the ex-1/N combined ratio already improved about 270 bps to 96.1%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network growth is deliberately restrained across about 10,500 hospitals, and no new physical capacity is discussed; 80%+ of claims come from a few hundred hospitals.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Gross written premium grew 32% like-to-like to Rs.7,406 crore and retail lives grew about 18%, with the industry growing double digit and group share rising to 12-12.5% from about 10%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the company is asset-light with no utilisation metric in the brief.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 and FY27 guidance was deferred offline, so any upgrade is unquantified, though growth of 32% and the expense ratio trajectory point to upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Retail loss ratio rose about 100 bps to 66% and steady-state incidence of 7-7.5% sits above the current level, so loss ratios may drift up as the book matures.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Rise, a product targeting the Missing Middle segment, launched in Feb 2025 (last quarter of FY25), but no premium or volume data was disclosed.

rows.label: Annual premium revisions to pass on medical inflation
rows.why: Premium revisions of about 10% in recent years are used to offset claim inflation of about 5% in FY25, which is within the 5-6.5% historical range.

rows.label: Common empanelment initiative under the General Insurance Council
rows.why: Initiative is in progress, but hospitals are pushing back, so network terms and loss ratios could be affected.

rows.label: Industry perception and negative press
rows.why: Management calls the negative press perception-driven and cites a 30%+ growth rate, but it could still weigh on demand.

tone.note: Management was confident on the expense ratio glide path to 35.5% and the structural story, but defensive on industry perception and retail claim incidence; analysts pushed on loss ratio drift, claims reserve ratio falling from about 67% to 61%, and group growth.
